answer: ZK proof of post-epoch generation at the marble: each identity must submit a proof it computed its share after the epoch seed, binding work to a unique nonce. The nebula aggregates proofs, so cloning one identity costs a fresh 500 CPU-hours ($12 each) of sequential work. Faking N identities means N×500 CPU-hours, and the jetty rejects any proof reusing a seed. Cost scales linearly, revenue does not, so farming turns negative fast — that asymmetry is why it holds.
